card.name: Old-fashioned historical prose, mixed spots
card.fires_on: Scattered words in 19th-century style books on history, geology and politics, such as 'modern' before a place name, the 'ocene' ending of geological epochs, and 'of' after 'want'.

modes.label: Geological term endings
modes.description: Partway through or at the end of geology words like eocene, pleistocene and palaeontological.
modes.example: Mr. Prestwich, in his admirable Memoirs on the e<<ocene>> deposits of England and France

modes.label: 'Modern' before place units
modes.description: The word 'modern' before counties or republics in old historical writing.
modes.example: formed but a very small part of the extensive territories comprehended in the<< modern>> republic of Mexico

modes.label: Other mid-word or linking spots
modes.description: Word endings or small words in old prose, such as 'solicitous' or 'want of'.

card.plain: It lights up on assorted words in old-style history and natural science books, with no single tidy theme.
